# Nettivibhāvinī (Tika S0501t)
**ID:** Tika S0501t
**Section:** Tikā Khuddakanikāya (tika-s05)
**Collection:** Tika-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Nettivibhāvinī
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Nettivibhāvinī* (also designated as the *Nettivibhāvinī-ṭīkā*) is a Pali sub-commentary belonging to the Ṭīkā Khuddakanikāya section of the Pali canon [von Hinüber 1994; Si Ti La 2014]. The work was composed by Saddhammapālasiri in fifteenth-century Burma as an exegetical commentary on the *Nettippakaraṇa* [von Hinüber 1994]. In modern scholarship, the text is cited for its grammatical and doctrinal analyses, such as Saddhammapālasiri's morphological interpretation of *upapajje* in *upapajjavedanīyā* (commenting on Nett 37,14) as the locative form of an abstract verbal noun or nominalized adjective [von Hinüber 1994]. It is also cited in comparative philological studies concerning karmic ripening across existences [Karashima 2012], as well as in doctrinal studies of Abhidhamma psychology for its glosses defining *adosa* (non-hatred) as the direct opponent of *dosa* (*dosassa paṭipakkho adoso*) and describing *taṇhāpema* (affection rooted in craving) (*chasu rūpādīsu pavattam taṇhāpemam*) [Si Ti La 2014].
There is no SuttaCentral entry or curated parallel list for the text [SuttaCentral]. According to machine analysis by DharmaNexus, the *Nettivibhāvinī* shares substantial Pali-internal text reuse with 451 other Pali works, yielding over 37,000 matching passages [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual reuse partners include the *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* (2,699 matches, with segments §391_5–421 corresponding to §223_8–251_0), the *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* of the *Nettippakaraṇa*, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Nettippakaraṇa-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with a score of 10 or greater are registered in the DharmaNexus database [DharmaNexus].
